title: Supported homogeneous division under complementary-variable perturbations
statement:
Let $L$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $m,r,s\ge0$, and use the polynomial rings $L[V_1,\ldots,V_r]$ and $L[U_1,\ldots,U_m,V_1,\ldots,V_r]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_s\in\mathbf N^r$ be distinct ordered vectors, $d_i=|\alpha_i|$, $D=\bigcup_i(\alpha_i+\mathbf N^r)$, and $\Delta_i=\{\beta:\alpha_i+\beta\notin\bigcup_{j<i}(\alpha_j+\mathbf N^r)\}$. Let $H_i(U,V)$ be homogeneous polynomials of total degree $d_i$, allowing zero polynomials, and put $h_i(V)=H_i(0,V)$. Then the following are equivalent:
(i) For every $t\ge0$, the indexed family $\{V^\beta h_i:\beta\in\Delta_i,\ |\beta|+d_i=t\}\amalg\{V^\gamma:\gamma\notin D,\ |\gamma|=t\}$ is an $L$-basis of the homogeneous degree-$t$ polynomials in $V$.
(ii) For every $t\ge0$, the indexed family $\{U^\mu V^\beta H_i:\beta\in\Delta_i,\ |\mu|+|\beta|+d_i=t\}\amalg\{U^\mu V^\gamma:\gamma\notin D,\ |\mu|+|\gamma|=t\}$ is an $L$-basis of the homogeneous degree-$t$ polynomials in $(U,V)$.
In the second family the orthant diagram is $\mathbf N^m\times D$ and the quotient supports are $\mathbf N^m\times\Delta_i$, so these are exactly the unique supported homogeneous division properties of [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]. No monotonicity of $D$ or first-exponent hypothesis on the $H_i$ is assumed. The equivalence remains valid after any extension of $L$, with the polynomials mapped coefficientwise; if the equivalent properties hold over $L$, they hold after every such extension. The empty vertex list, either empty variable list, and a vertex of degree zero are included.

source.place: Route: VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94. Detailed algebraic input: Bierstone--Milman, Canonical desingularization in characteristic zero, Invent. Math. 128 (1997), Lemma 7.7, printed pp.263--264, implication (c) to (a) and its converse; degree-by-degree formulation. Read online at https://mahalex.net/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf; BM is WANTED locally. No Stacks tag states this supported division comparison.

proof.text: Fix $t$. Assign a generator index $(i,\beta)$ to $\alpha_i+\beta$ and a remainder index $\gamma$ to $\gamma$. Every exponent in $D$ lies in exactly one first orthant: take the least $i$ with $\alpha_i\le\gamma$ coordinatewise, then $\beta=\gamma-\alpha_i\in\Delta_i$. Conversely this assignment determines $i,\beta$ uniquely. It preserves degree. Thus the degree-$t$ restricted index set bijects with the degree-$t$ monomials in $V$. The all-variable index set bijects with the degree-$t$ monomials in $(U,V)$ by keeping $\mu$. Both are finite, since every coordinate is at most $t$. Adding zero $U$ coordinates to the vertices gives precisely $\mathbf N^m\times D$ and $\mathbf N^m\times\Delta_i$. These are the supported quotient and remainder indices in [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]; only its indexed-family definition is used, not its monotonicity or finite-test conditions.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, for the resolution route; algebra refinement of Bierstone--Milman 1997, Lemma 7.7, pp.263--264 (online PDF in source.place; WANTED locally). The argument below is written by Q41.

proof.text: Assume (i). Every homogeneous degree-$t$ polynomial has a unique expression $\sum_{|\mu|\le t}U^\mu p_\mu(V)$, where $p_\mu$ is homogeneous of degree $t-|\mu|$: group its monomials by their $U$ exponent. Expand each $p_\mu$ uniquely in the basis from (i) for that degree. Comparing $U$ coefficients proves both spanning and independence. Hence the unperturbed family $B_t^0=\{U^\mu V^\beta h_i\}\amalg\{U^\mu V^\gamma\}$, with exactly the indices of (ii), is a basis. This coefficient argument uses the finite monomial expansion of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring].

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, for the resolution route; algebra refinement of Bierstone--Milman 1997, Lemma 7.7, pp.263--264 (online PDF in source.place; WANTED locally). The argument below is written by Q41.

proof.text:
Order the finite indices of $B_t^0$ by increasing $|\mu|$, breaking ties arbitrarily. The difference of the perturbed generator and its corresponding old basis vector is $U^\mu V^ eta(H_i-h_i)$. Each monomial of $H_i-h_i$ has positive $U$ degree. Grouping this difference by $U^
u$, its nonzero coefficients have $|
u|>|\mu|$ and are homogeneous in $V$ of degree $t-|
u|$. Expand each coefficient in the corresponding restricted basis from (i), exactly as in step 2. Thus each new vector equals its old vector plus a combination of old vectors strictly later in this order. Remainder vectors are unchanged. The coordinate matrix is triangular with diagonal $1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-triangular-change-of-basis], with $R=L$, the degree-$t$ polynomial space as the free module, and $B_t^0$ as its basis (enumerate the finite index set). Its unit-diagonal hypotheses hold. The resulting basis is exactly (ii).

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, for the resolution route; algebra refinement of Bierstone--Milman 1997, Lemma 7.7, pp.263--264 (online PDF in source.place; WANTED locally). The argument below is written by Q41.

proof.text: Assume (ii). Express a degree-$t$ polynomial $p(V)$ in its full basis and set $U=0$. Terms with $\mu\ne0$ vanish and those with $\mu=0$ become exactly the restricted family, since $H_i(0,V)=h_i(V)$. Thus the restricted family spans. Step 1 bijects its indices with the monomial basis of the same degree. Send each monomial basis vector to the corresponding restricted vector, giving a surjective endomorphism of this finite free $L$-module. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-surjective-endomorphism-bijective]; $L$ is commutative and the finite monomial basis supplies finite generation. The endomorphism is injective too, so the restricted indexed family is independent and is a basis. This proves (i) for every $t$.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, for the resolution route; algebra refinement of Bierstone--Milman 1997, Lemma 7.7, pp.263--264 (online PDF in source.place; WANTED locally). The argument below is written by Q41.

proof.text: For a field embedding $L\to E$, each fixed-degree family is the same finite square coefficient matrix, now mapped into $E$, in the monomial bases of step 1. If it is a basis over $L$, its inverse matrix also has entries in $L$; mapping both matrices to $E$ preserves the two inverse identities, so it is a basis over $E$. This proves preservation for either equivalent property. The arguments in steps 1--4 apply over the field $E$ itself, proving the equivalence there whether or not the properties held over $L$. Grouping the generator coefficients by $i$ gives the quotient supported in $\mathbf N^m\times\Delta_i$, and the remaining coefficients the remainder outside $\mathbf N^m\times D$; uniqueness of basis coefficients is exactly uniqueness of these supported homogeneous polynomials.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, for the resolution route; algebra refinement of Bierstone--Milman 1997, Lemma 7.7, pp.263--264 (online PDF in source.place; WANTED locally). The argument below is written by Q41.

proof.text: No step requires a first exponent or monotonicity. If $s=0$, $D$ is empty and both families are the full monomial families. If $m=0$, the families coincide; if $r=0$, the only $V$ exponent is $0$ and step 1 still applies. A degree-zero vertex has $H_i=h_i$ constant, so its perturbation difference is zero; if its constant vanishes and its index occurs, the zero vector prevents both properties. A zero $H_i$ whose quotient support is nonempty prevents both basis assertions in a degree containing one of its indices; if that support is empty, it contributes no vector to either family. Empty degree components use the empty basis and the zero-module endomorphism; degree zero uses the constant monomial. All stated degenerate cases are therefore included.
